sentences.text: This is the second bail application.
First was rejected by a reasoned order dated 20.1.2021 and relevant part thereof is mentioned hereinafter:
"From the material on record and DNA report, it is evident that the applicant has prima-facie committed the offence of rape and he is the father of the child.

The offence against the applicant is of a serious nature, in case of bail, possibility of influencing the victim and other material witnesses could not be ruled out, therefore,
no case is made out for bail, hence this bail application is rejected.
However, the applicant is at liberty to approach this Court under Section 483 Cr.P.C. with the prayer to expedite the trial."

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri P.S. Chauhan, Advocate holding brief of Sri Gaurav Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Mithilesh Kumar, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

3. The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application in Case Crime No.252 of 2019 under Sections 376 (3), 506 I.P.C. and Section 5 J (II),
(K) (L)/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station-Jansath, District-Muzaffar Nagar.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that statement of victim has already been recorded and she has made material contradictions so much as that prosecution may not be able to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt.
Age of the victim as per her ossification test was opined to be between 16-17 years, as such benefit of two years could be granted in favour of applicant.

Medical evidence also has not supported the case of prosecution and there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial and the applicant undertakes that if enlarged on bail, he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.
5. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application and submits that victim's statement before learned Trial Court was consistent and is against the applicant.
At this stage even on the basis of her Ossification Test, it could not be held that victim was a major girl since her age was opined to be between 16-17 years.

6.I have considered the above mentioned rival submissions in referred factual and legal background and in view of established principle of jurisprudence of bail i.e 'bail is rule and jail is exception' as well as relevant factors for consideration of a bail application such as (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence; (ii) nature and gravity of the accusation; (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv) danger of the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means, position and standing of the accused;(vi) likelihood of the offence being repeated; (vii) reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being influenced; (viii) danger of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail etc. and that an order to grant or not to grant bail must assigned reasons (see Deepak Yadav Vs.
State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 559, Manoj Kumar Khokar Vs. State of Rajasthan and Anr (2022) 3 SCC 501, The State of Jharkhand Vs. Dhananjay Gupta @ Dhananjay Prasad Gupta: Order dated 7.11.2023 in SLP (Crl) No.10810/2023 and Shiv Kumar Vs The State of U.P. and Ors: Order dated 12.9.2023 in Criminal Appeal No.2782 of 2023; Ramayan Singh Vs. The State of U.P. and Anr, 2024 SCC Online SC 563), therefore, I am of considered opinion that present is not a fit case to grant bail to applicant mainly on following reasons:-

sentences.text: (i) In the aforesaid circumstances, taking note of nature of evidence i.e. statement of victim which appears to be against the applicant as well as taking note that delay was caused since applicant has not cross-examined P.W.1 and P.W.2 and his application to recall P.W.2 under Section 311 Cr.P.C. was rejected and other application to recall P.W.2 was pending as on 10.5.2024, as such delay was on part of applicant.
( ii )

Court also takes note that during pendency of first bail application, applicant was granted interim bail on 18.1.2020 and it appears that he has surrendered thereafter Rajpal Saini vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18828913/
2 one year, as such period of incarceration would be of three years and eight months and not four years and eight months (since 12.8.2019).

entities.text: Rajpal Saini vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. This second bail application is accordingly rejected.

However, considering the period of incarceration and that trial is still not concluded, therefore, it is directed that learned Trial Court will take all endeavour to conclude the trial expeditiously, if there is no other legal impediment and in case it has not substantially progressed within a period of eight months, applicant will be at liberty to approach this Court or learned Trial Court as advised alongwith status of trial.
8. Registrar (Compliance) to take steps.
